detailed_findings.finding: Existence of each w_i is justified from finiteness of the complement, by showing every sufficiently large number in the residue class i mod m lies in S.
The argument that x_i is positive is correct: w_i is a positive element of S not congruent to 0 mod m, hence at least m, and x_i <= 0 would force w_i < m.
The representation of every s in S as either 0, a multiple of m, or w_i plus a nonnegative multiple of m is complete and uses minimality of w_i appropriately.
detailed_findings.location: Forward direction, equality description of S

detailed_findings.finding: Both Kunz inequalities are derived correctly from closure and minimality of the appropriate Apéry representative; the omission of the i+j=m case is consistent with the statement.
In the converse direction, finite complement and multiplicity m are established correctly from positivity of the x_i and the explicit residue-class description.
detailed_findings.location: Converse direction, finite complement and multiplicity

detailed_findings.finding: Closure under addition for S_x is handled by a full and correct case split, including the necessary special case i+j=m.

reason: The proof correctly establishes both directions of the Kunz-coordinate characterization at multiplicity m. In the forward direction it proves existence/minimality of each Apéry representative w_i, derives positivity of x_i, proves the exact decomposition of S by residue classes mod m, and derives the two stated Kunz inequalities from minimality of the corresponding Apéry representatives. In the converse direction it defines S_x, proves finite complement, verifies closure under addition by a complete residue-class case split (including the i+j=m case needed for closure), and checks that no positive element below m lies in S_x while m does, yielding multiplicity m. The proof matches the semantic sketch with no substantive omissions or drift.
